clue.text: Countryman at university reported in temporary difficulty

indicators.note: reported means the clue's pieces are to be heard spoken rather than read on the page

parts.note: a countryman is a HICK, and being at university is being UP; together they are spoken

explanation.surface: A rustic student finds himself in a spot of bother, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' signals that HICK + UP said aloud gives the word, which has the alternative spelling with -COUGH. 'Up' meaning in residence at university is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief interruption or setback is figuratively called a hiccup, as in a hitch in plans.

clue.text: Press magnate tries to forget love

parts.note: a court hears, or tries, a case

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A newspaper owner attempts to put romance out of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forget' drops the O from HEARSTO, leaving the surname of the American publisher William Randolph Hearst.
explanation.definitionFit: William Randolph Hearst built a huge American newspaper empire, a classic tycoon of the newspapers.

clue.text: Reduce size of committee giving support for writers

parts.note: to clip is to trim or cut down
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A downsized panel still backs its authors.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipboard is a stiff backing that holds paper steady while someone writes on it.

clue.text: Monument to honour sinister king is captured

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

indicators.note: captured means the word is is held within the left-and-king letters

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, abbreviated L
K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A memorial honouring an evil monarch who has been taken prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone pillar raised as a memorial.

clue.text: The low-down on soldiers' literary style

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the low-down
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: The inside story on the troops' preferred kind of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or type of literary work, such as crime fiction.

clue.text: Plant established by one in command in the vineyards

indicators.note: in tells us the commander's letters sit within the vineyard word

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine; plural CRUS
OC is the abbreviation for officer commanding

explanation.surface: A flower planted by the officer in charge among the vines.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring-flowering bulb is a garden flower, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Old recipe for pie turning up in corrective centre

indicators.note: in places the turned pie letters within the central letters
centre asks for the middle four letters of the word corrective
in a down clue turning up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

explanation.surface: An old pie recipe surfaces at a reform institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old recipe' is the definition, since this was once the usual word for a recipe; 'turning up' reverses 'pie', and 'centre' takes the middle four letters of 'corrective', not just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipt was the standard word for a cooking formula until the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Assets orginally held in the Channel Islands — or raised in the capital

indicators.note: held in means the initial letter is placed within the islands' abbreviation

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

indicators.note: orginally (as printed) means the first letter of the word assets is taken
in a down clue raised means the word is turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Money stashed offshore in Jersey or Guernsey, or else raised in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands (Jersey, Guernsey) are a British tax haven, which suits 'assets'. 'raised' turns OR into RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Visit places of interest in York, for instance, after the show

indicators.note: after places the York piece following the show piece

parts.note: a sight is a spectacle or show
York is the seat of an archbishop, a see

explanation.surface: A tourist goes round York after seeing a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourists tour monuments and attractions, which is the activity described.

clue.text: Abstract a key, perhaps

explanation.surface: A summary, perhaps of an important point.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare outline of a work is an abstract, and a skeleton key opens many locks.

clue.text: Very active naval king — that's Dick!

annotationWithheld.why: Very active naval king — that's Dick! (5,3,7): letters are an anagram of NAVAL KING + IE (that's) + DICK, but no separate word signals the anagram; 'active' would have to be both definition and indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Very active naval king — that's Dick!

clue.text: Boat possibly left to sink

parts.note: a sub (submarine) is a boat
the left is one example of a side

explanation.surface: A vessel, perhaps abandoned, is allowed to go under.
explanation.definitionFit: To subside is to settle lower or go down, as ground or floodwater does.

clue.text: Spent money as arranged

explanation.surface: Someone paid out cash as agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out cash is to spend it, and things set out in order are arranged neatly.

clue.text: Player put in position of inferior status

parts.note: a back is a defending player in football or rugby
to seat someone is to put them in place

explanation.surface: A sportsman is moved to a lowly spot in the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a back seat idiomatically means accepting a subordinate role.

clue.text: Rise late, dishevelled but first

indicators.note: dishevelled means untidy, so the letters are messed into a new order

explanation.surface: Get up late, unkempt, yet still be ahead of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The soonest or initial of several things comes before all others.

clue.text: Leitmotif in Goethe melodrama

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: A recurring musical idea in a dramatic work by the German poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurring idea or subject in a work, its central motif.

clue.text: Even one's editor can be made to correspond

parts.note: even means level or equal
one's is I'S, the Roman numeral I with 's

explanation.surface: Even someone's editor can be brought into line.
explanation.definitionFit: Things evened up so that they match are made level or equivalent.

clue.text: Shepherds harm lass, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given may be reworked into another form

explanation.surface: Sheep farmers might hurt a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal people is to guide or herd them into order, a verbal sense of shepherding.

clue.text: A dreadfully difficult unsolved problem starts to make sense

indicators.note: starts tells us to take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A fiendish unsolved puzzle begins to become clear.
explanation.definitionFit: When an explanation adds up it is coherent and consistent, so it is understandable.

clue.text: Mean offer

explanation.surface: A stingy proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to intend (one's meaning or plan) and also to put forward a suggestion.

clue.text: Dealers getting together certainly sound credible

parts.note: a ring is a group of dealers colluding to fix prices
true! is an exclamation of agreement, meaning certainly

explanation.surface: Merchants meeting up surely seem believable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rings true has the convincing tone of honesty, so seems believable.

clue.text: A tedious walk for unfortunate pirates

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests the sea robbers' letters meet a bad end and get scrambled

explanation.surface: Walking the plank is a dreary stroll for luckless buccaneers.
explanation.definitionFit: A traipse is a long, wearisome trudge.

clue.text: Diseased and worthless

explanation.surface: Sick and useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly literally means infected with the measles virus, and colloquially paltry or contemptible.

clue.text: Retired soldier admitted to clubs for men in Rome

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
admitted to means the soldier's letters are let inside the clubs word

parts.note: irons are golf clubs
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An old serviceman gets membership of gentlemen's clubs in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired soldier' looks like one veteran, but 'Retired' reverses the whole build, with 'admitted to' placing the soldier inside the golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian plural for gentlemen, used as the title Mr.

clue.text: Agreement about, for example, climbing the Lizard

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the whole run is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OK expresses agreement
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A deal reached about scaling the cliffs at the Cornish headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns OKCEG upward. The Lizard is a peninsula in Cornwall, England, which the capital L disguises.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small climbing reptile, one kind of lizard.

clue.text: A fish — a whopper — for a fool!

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: An angler's tall tale makes him look silly.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is British slang for a silly person, an idiot.

clue.text: Express analysis made on this

explanation.surface: Rapid psychoanalysis is carried out here.
explanation.definitionFit: To couch something is to phrase it, and the psychoanalyst's patient lies on a sofa during treatment.

clue.text: Silly ass procures stop in mutual conflict

indicators.note: silly suggests the following letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A foolish donkey brings things to a halt in a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: People at cross purposes misunderstand one another, working against each other's aims.

clue.text: Drab quarters give a home to charity

indicators.note: give a home to means the first letters take in and enclose the second

parts.note: S and N, south and north, are compass quarters
charity in the biblical sense is love

explanation.surface: Dreary lodgings take in a good cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A drab is an old word for a slovenly woman, so a slattern or untidy person.

clue.text: "The air bites —— ; it is very cold" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "The air bites —— ; it is very cold" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "The air bites —— ; it is very cold" (Hamlet)
parts.note: a quotation from the battlements scene with a word missing after bites; the gap is the adverb Shakespeare used, meaning keenly or sharply

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: the dash on the page marks where the word goes in Hamlet's line on the cold night watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Here the adverb means keenly or piercingly, an older sense than its usual one of cleverly.
